newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end just off highs,hope of metal deal.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end just off highs,hope of metal deal.

text.p: Italian shares ended firm on Tuesday, just off session highs, boosted by hopes of an imminent deal in the long-running metalworkers pay conflict as all unions say they back a government proposal to end the dispute, traders said.

The market extended gains in the afternoon, apparently ignoring the fact Wall Street was off with bonds as investors awaited the outcome of a two-day FOMC meeting ending Wednesday, and ahead of U.S. January jobs data Friday.
The All-share Mibtel index closed up 0.99 percent at 12,411 after 12,421 high and the Mib30 blue chip index ended 1.02 percent higher at 18,448 after 18,473.
Volume was seen good at around one trillion lire.
"It's a strong market which held up well despite tension over EMU polemics," one trader said. "But we are still seeing few foreign buyers," he added.
Olivetti ended sharply higher after reported interest from Bell Atlantic and France Telecom in the businesses of the hi-tech group. Olivetti closed 3.35 percent up at 670 lire after a high at 677.
Financial holding Gemina put on 2.78 percent to 991 lire as market awaits the debut of its HPI industrial conglomerate. Fiat rose 1.79 percent to 5,350 lire.

In firmer banks, buying continued on Credito Italiano after the stock surged on Monday on good 1996 results. The stock ended 3.35 percent up at 2,345. Banca Fideuram rose 4.91 percent to 4,640 and Banca Commerciale Italiana put on 4.35 percent to 3,355.
Operators were looking to monthly data on investment fund inflows due on Thursday for confirmation of December figures showing cash and interest switching into equities from bonds.
Telecoms were neglected. Telecom Italy put on a modest 0.02 percent gain to 4,512, mobile phone operator TIM rose 0.4 percent to 4,721 and Stet holding gained 0.61 percent to 7,885.
